title: Switching the active profile is only possible by changing which profile launches at startup
summary: Already closed in this shard's working tree; I confirmed it by revert. ProfileSidebar takes an onActivateProfile callback and watches activeEquipmentProfileProvider, so selected and active are distinct states. The footer of a selected-but-not-active profile leads with a primary 'Use This Profile' button (Connect All demotes to outline there — two primaries side by side is no emphasis at all), and the same action heads the per-profile menu. Every card now carries a visible '...' overflow button (profileCardMenuButtonKey) opening the menu that used to be right-click only. The star is relabelled to say what it actually controls: 'Make Startup Default' / 'Startup Default' instead of 'Set as Default', which read as 'use this one' and was the only route anyone found to switching rigs — while silently rewriting every future launch.

title: The optical-train step asks the user to look up a pixel size the driver already reports
summary: Two halves. (a) Pixel size: the camera step now resolves the driver-reported camera name through the shipped camera library (hardwarePresetsService.matchCameraByName) and seeds draft.pixelSizeMicrons, only on an actual camera CHANGE so a hand-typed value survives re-selecting the same camera, and only on a match so an unknown camera prefills nothing rather than guessing. The optical-train field's placeholder stopped saying 'Look this up in your camera spec sheet' and a provenance line under it names where a prefilled number came from ('Filled in from ZWO ASI2600MM Pro in the camera library (IMX571)'), disappearing the moment the user types something else. That code was already in this shard's tree but had NO test; I wrote one. (b) The second camera identification: step 9 offered only 'Choose from camera library', so the operator hunted for the same camera again. It now leads with a one-tap 'Use <camera> settings' button built from the same match, retiring once a preset is applied. Deliberately a tap, not a silent write — gain and offset are the imager's call and the library only recommends.

title: The capture-folder step offers no way to type a path
summary: The folder row was a read-only Text beside a single Browse button, so the native directory chooser was the only way to answer the step — no way to paste `/mnt/nvme/astro` or a UNC share, and the worst possible control on an appliance driven over VNC. Settings > Files & Storage already accepts a typed path for this exact setting (image_output_path), so the wizard that sets it FIRST was the odd one out. The row is now a real TextField that commits on Enter and on focus loss (tabbing away is how people leave a path box), routed through the same existence + writability check the picker's result goes through. The draft is written only once the check passes, so a typo cannot become the answer that unblocks Next; the rejected text stays in the box to be corrected rather than retyped. Remote mode still asks the host, via the existing _verify path. Browse is unchanged.

title: Equipment Settings mixes auto-save and Apply-required sections and repeats its own title
summary: Two parts. (a) The duplicated heading was already removed in this shard's tree (both hosts — the desktop SkotiqDialog and the phone AppBar — already render 'Equipment Settings' directly above the body, and repeating it cost a heading's worth of the dialog's fixed height). (b) The save-model mismatch: Camera/Mount/Focuser save on edit while Built-in Guider alone has Reset/Apply, with nothing saying which is which. Making the guider save on edit would be wrong — it pushes eight interdependent numbers to a guider that may be running right now, and a half-typed max-pulse reaching a live mount is exactly what an atomic Apply prevents — so the difference is now structural rather than remembered: Apply is live ONLY while the fields differ from the config the guider is actually running, a warning-toned 'Not applied yet — press Apply to send these to the guider.' line appears alongside the existing 'Last applied:' line while anything is pending, and the section description states the Apply contract. Typing a value back to its stored value clears the pending state, so the warning never cries wolf.

title: INDI and Alpaca startup discovery default to off after the wizard offered them as scan backends
summary: The driver step's answer is now stored, not thrown away. `OnboardingNotifier.complete()` used to persist only the capture directory; the `selectedDrivers` set steered the wizard's own discovery passes and then died with the draft, while Settings > Equipment > Connection asked the same question again through 'Query INDI/Alpaca on startup' (both default false). A user who found their camera over INDI during onboarding got an app that never queried INDI at launch again. `_persistAppSettings` now writes imageOutputPath, indi_auto_connect and alpaca_auto_discover together — one read-modify-write on a remote host so a second round trip cannot drop the field it did not carry. Both flags are written, not just the true ones, so unticking INDI can take an inherited `true` away. An empty driver set (a draft restored from before the step existed) leaves both toggles alone rather than answering for the user.

title: Discovery says only that no switches or cover calibrators were found, without saying why or what to do
summary: Already closed in this shard's working tree; I confirmed it by revert. Zero-result classes get the same section chrome as every other class — titled header, icon, and an honest '0 found' count instead of one bare italic line — plus a body that names the backends actually searched and any that errored, or 'Not searched yet — run a scan.' before the first scan, and a route to configuring a remote server. The information already existed (the app log recorded 'Discovery complete for Switch: 0 devices, 0 backend errors'); the section that says nothing was found is where it belongs.
